finding.claim: Duplicate id values overwrite earlier subjects, so the <use> expansion threshold checks the last element with an id while renderers expand the first. An exponential billion-laughs chain bypasses useThreshold.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled SVG with repeated id attributes; expensive <g id=l_i> elements appear first and empty decoy <g id=l_i/> elements appear later.
finding.sink: Renderer expansion of <use xlink:href="#l_N"/> to the first element in document order (unbounded exponential expansion).

trace.note: collectIdentifiedElements queries //*[@id] in document order.
subjects[id] is overwritten by each later duplicate, so only the last element survives.
processReferences iterates only $this->subjects, so <use> inside shadowed elements are never added to the graph.
findByElementId returns only the surviving subject.
isUseTagExceedingThreshold resolves the target via findByElementId.
Threshold check runs countUse on the decoy, which has zero uses.
Threshold check is invoked for each <use> element; the decoy passes.

finding.guards_checked: useThreshold (Sanitizer.php:57, 683) is bypassed because the count is taken from the wrong element. The nesting limit (Subject.php:60-67) is skipped for shadowed subjects. isUseTagDirty (Sanitizer.php:667-671) passes because the references are internal '#' links. Repro is by reading only; not executed.

finding.claim: Cycle marking clears the wrong nodes. The cycle a<->b survives into countUse, which recurses without a cycle guard, causing unbounded recursion and a fatal error on a single small file.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled SVG: <g id=s> with <use> to #a and #b; <g id=a> with <use> to #b; <g id=b> with <use> to #a; top-level <use xlink:href="#a"/>.
finding.sink: Subject::countUse() recursion through useCollection (memory exhaustion or fatal error in the sanitizer process).

trace.note: hasInfiniteLoop on subject s returns true via a->b->a.
markSubjectAsInvalid(s) returns elements of s's targets (a, b) for removal.
clearInternalAndGetAffectedElements clears only s's own out-edges.
Subjects a and b are skipped because their elements are now in elementsToRemove, so their a->b and b->a edges remain.
startClean walks children in reverse; the top-level <use href=#a> is checked first.
findByElementId('a') then countUse() on a.
countUse recurses a->b->a->... with no visited set and no depth limit.

finding.guards_checked: The nesting limit is only in hasInfiniteLoop (Subject.php:62); countUse has no equivalent. The cycle check cleared the wrong nodes. Repro is by reading only; not executed.

finding.claim: Self-referencing <use> (a direct child referencing its parent's id) and non-single-svg roots throw uncaught LogicException from sanitize(), which is documented to return string|false. The CLI has no try/catch, so one malicious file aborts the whole batch.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled SVG: <svg><g id=s><use xlink:href="#s"/></g></svg>. Separately any well-formed non-svg root such as <foo/>.
finding.sink: Uncaught LogicException escaping the library API and terminating the CLI process.

trace.note: new XPath() runs handleDefaultNamespace for non-svg roots.
Throws LogicException when root svg count is not exactly one.
processReferences finds the direct child use referencing its parent's id.
Calls $subject->addUse($subject).
addUse throws LogicException 'Cannot add self usage'.
No try/catch around the resolver; exception escapes sanitize().
CLI calls sanitize() with no try/catch; the batch aborts.

finding.guards_checked: Only loadXML failure is handled (Sanitizer.php:237-241). On the exception path, resetAfter() is skipped, leaving libxml error-handling state changed. Verified by reading.

finding.claim: hasRemoteReference requires quotes inside url(), so unquoted url(https://...) is not detected. removeRemoteReferences (enabled by the CLI) fails to strip remote paint, filter, or mask references.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled attribute value such as fill="url(https://attacker.example/x.svg#p)" on any allowed element.
finding.sink: Renderer or browser fetch of the remote resource (SSRF-like fetch or tracking when rendered server-side).

trace.note: removeRemoteReferences branch runs only when the option is enabled.
hasRemoteReference is called on the attribute value.
Pattern requires [' or "] after url( and before ); unquoted url() never matches.
Returns false, so the attribute is kept.
CLI enables removeRemoteReferences(true), so the bypass affects the scanner.

finding.guards_checked: removeNonPrintableCharacters (Sanitizer.php:594) does not help with unquoted URLs. Default removeRemoteReferences is false (Sanitizer.php:52). Verified by reading.

finding.claim: Subtree handling for <use> does not cover CSS in <style> text or style attributes. Remote CSS (@import url(...), or url(//host) inside style="fill:url(...)") is kept even when removeRemoteReferences is on, and <style> is a global-scope CSS injection vector when inlined into HTML.
finding.sink: Remote CSS fetch, data exfiltration via attribute selectors, or global page CSS if the SVG is inlined into HTML.

trace.note: style is an allowed tag.
Child nodes of allowed elements are recursed; text children are kept by cleanUnsafeNodes.
hasRemoteReference is applied only to attribute values, not to element text.
Whole-value url( anchor means style="fill:url(...)" never matches.

finding.guards_checked: The allowlist controls tag names and attribute names but not CSS content. Remote-reference removal is attribute-only. Verified by reading.
